title: Tenant ecoregion slowpath isolation and soft-park emergency stabilization
author: Priya Mukherjee
release_notes: Adds tenant ecoregion slowpath isolation and a soft-park mechanism to reduce SLO violations during KV pressure; configurable via serving.runtime.ecoregion and scheduler.soft_park.*
description: Summary: Introduces a serving-side scheduler extension that groups tenants into lightweight 'ecoregions' (region + workload fingerprint) and isolates slowpath/large-KV sessions into a soft-park queue when node-level KV pressure threatens SLOs. Motivation: During the Jan incident we observed correlated KV-heavy warm sessions from multiple tenants in the same AZ causing tail latency spikes and subsequent SLO breaches for unrelated low-latency tenants. This change provides a fast mitigation: (1) detect sustained KV pressure per-node and per-ecoregion, (2) move new/remaining slowpath requests for affected ecoregions into a soft-park state (deferred processing + light-weight token), (3) prioritize unmoved requests to preserve 95th/99th latency for interactive tenants, and (4) expose observability + an operator rollback. This PR is scoped for runtime safety and is intended as an emergency stabilization feature that is off by default and gated by config. What changed (high-level): - New scheduler module: serving/scheduler/ecoregion_scheduler.go (ecoregion detection, scoring, admission decisions) - New soft-park runtime: serving/runtime/soft_park.go (park queue, lightweight lease, KV-pressure circuit hooks) - Config knobs: config/defaults.yaml (serving.runtime.ecoregion.enabled=false by default, thresholds, park timeouts) - Metrics & telemetry: metrics/slo_tags.go, console/widgets/ecoregion-telemetry-panel.json - Integration tests: tests/integration/ecoregion_integration_test.go - Operator docs: docs/operating/ecoregion.md Why it's safe: - Feature is opt-in (serving.runtime.ecoregion.enabled=false) and guarded by two-tier checks (node_kv_pressure && ecoregion_spike_score). - Soft-park holds requests with a short, configurable lease (default 5s) that can be expired or promoted; requests are not dropped. - We add a rollout monitor check that will auto-disable the feature if error rates increase > 0.5 percentage points for any tenant in the group during warmup. Rollback plan: immediate toggle via runtime config (console + CLI) to revert to previous behavior. Fast rollback script included in scripts/rollbacks/disable_ecoregion.sh (not changing infra templates). Testing: - Unit tests for scheduler heuristics and soft-park transitions. - Integration tests simulate mixed workloads (low-latency chat + KV-heavy batch) and assert 95p latency preservation for low-latency tenants while soft-parked ecoregions show bounded increased tail. - Canary on dedicated infra: rolled to one canary pool for 12 hours, monitored SLO_ECO_95 and SLO_GLOBAL_99. CI history: initial CI run failed lint (naming) and a flaky integration test; fixed by commit 4 and rerun — final CI passed all checks (build, unit, integration, linters, telemetry smoke). Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (Linear ENG-4219) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary rollout completed (1 pool) - [x] Ops doc and console panel - [x] Runtime toggle + rollback script - [x] Metrics and alert hooks (SLO_ECO_95, ECO_SOFTPARK_INFLIGHT) Commits: see commit list below. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-27 after approvals. Related: SUP-1123 (customer incident), ENG-4231 (follow-up telemetry work).
